thread:
maria: follow-up from RFC review: i'm worried about cross-lane state leaks when we do aggressive reshuffles. proposal: a reshuffle-safe pathway that services must opt into. sketch below.

aj: +1 on defining an opt-in. can you summarize the failure mode again so we all have the same picture?

maria: failure mode: compacting moves requests between microwindows and changes the ordering seen by the scheduler. two consequences: (1) tenants that relied on enqueue-order see p99 spikes, (2) kv-cache warm affinity breaks, causing extra stalls.

kevin: saw this in load tests: a compacted tenant A gets coalesced with B's batch, A's kv keys miss and latency doubles for some requests.

sara: how is reshuffle-safe different from the compact-pathway we talked about earlier?

maria: reshuffle-safe is more prescriptive: queue exposes explicit "strict" and "reshuffle" lanes. reshuffle lane guarantees bounded perturbation: only within window W and only across requests with compaction_hint. strict lane preserves FIFO.

aj: sounds good. what are the knobs we need? window W, max-moved-requests, and per-tenant opt-in. also need an escape: if we can't meet SLO we avoid reshuffle.

maria: agreed. initial knobs: W_ms, max_moves, compaction_level {none, gentle, aggressive}. default route config = none (strict).

kevin: practical defaults? my experiments suggest W=25ms for small (<512 tokens), W=75ms for larger. max_moves=16 is a reasonable start.

sara: we also need a migration path for existing jobs. legacy callers currently expect ordering. adapter should map to strict by default. new SDK can expose request.compaction_hint.

maria: yes. adapter + feature-flagged route configs. header fallback: X-Redwood-Compaction: v1:<level>. but proto field is primary.

aj: telemetry is critical. propose metrics: compact_event{route,tenant,level}, reshuffle_distance (count & med_bytes), post_compaction_latency_delta (p50/p99), kv_cache_miss_rate_delta. gate rollouts on no-regress for 7d.

kevin: add synthetic canary: create dedicated synthetic tenant that exercises canary prompts and route X% of traffic to reshuffle lanes. collect both perf and model quality diffs.

sara: test matrix: mixed small/big workloads, streaming + small interactive, tenant isolation vs multi-tenant pool. ensure reshuffle doesn't starve long streams.

maria: good. one constraint: reshuffle must not cross tenant boundaries. compaction only operates within same-tenant groups or pinned multi-tenant pools where mixing is allowed. billing attribution must remain per-request.

aj: implementation: do we put reshuffle logic in queue or scheduler? queue seems easier for adapter and local guarantees; scheduler can do global packing but complicates ordering SLOs.

maria: leaning queue-side. queue can expose two enqueue APIs: enqueue_strict(req) and enqueue_reshuffle(req). scheduler will read a reshuffle_hint and treat reshuffled requests as having potential order variance.

kevin: if queue handles it, ensure we also emit an event when a reshuffle actually moves a request: "reshuffle_applied" with before/after index. telemetry folks can correlate.

sara: small API proto sample (pseudo):

```
message Request {
  string route = 1;
  bytes payload = 2;
  enum CompactionHint { NONE = 0; GENTLE = 1; AGGRESSIVE = 2; }
  CompactionHint compaction_hint = 3;
}
queue.enqueue(Request req);
```

maria: perfect. note: do not rely on headers for primary semantics. proxies drop headers. header only for legacy.

aj: version compatibility: queue should accept missing compaction_hint and treat as NONE. new compaction header should be ignored when proto field present. version the header as X-Redwood-Compaction: v1.

kevin: operational concern: CPU jitter from reshuffling code path under high throughput. we should benchmark cost of reshuffle in the hot path and maybe offload heavier heuristics to a batch coalescer thread.

sara: and add a circuit breaker: if reshuffle CPU > threshold, autoscale or disable aggressive-mode automatically.

maria: rollout checklist i'll include in RFC PR: (1) queue API + proto change behind feature flag, (2) adapter maps legacy to strict, (3) metrics & histograms, (4) synthetic canary tenant + canary orchestration, (5) stress tests + mixed workload matrix, (6) auto-disable circuit breaker, (7) docs + SDK examples.

aj: can you add a short blurb on acceptance criteria? what does "no-regress" mean quantitatively?

maria: acceptance: for canary tenants, p99 latency delta <= 5% vs baseline and kv_cache_miss_rate delta <= 2% for 7d; CPU overhead of reshuffle path < 3% of service baseline. if any fail, rollback.

infra-bot: deploy-preview: branch "reshuffle-safe/proto-v1" created, smoke-run queued.

kevin: i'll take ownership of stress tests and microbenchmarks. sara can own telemetry dashboards. aj, want to review the rollout playbook?

aj: yes, ping me.

maria: thanks everyone. i'll open the follow-up RFC + PR with the proto diff and the rollout checklist. ping me if you want to be reviewer. :rocket:
